neighbours.label: The close of a sentence-opening justification phrase that gives the basis for what follows ('As the name implies,', 'For safety reasons,', 'For convenience,', 'Out of habit,'); quiet at the comma of a fronted time or place phrase (the + pole's side)
fire: As its name implies, the snowshoe hare has very large hind feet.
For practical reasons, the meeting will be held in the smaller hall.
As the label indicates, this cheese must be kept below five degrees.
For convenience, the tables in this chapter use metric units only.
Out of habit, he still checks the mailbox every morning.
As the nickname suggests, the old locomotive was painted bright green.
For reasons of space, only the first ten entries are printed here.
Because of an old injury, she avoids running on hard pavement.
quiet: When the snow melts, the hare loses its white winter coat.
On Thursday evening, the meeting will be held in the smaller hall.
Once opened, this cheese must be kept below five degrees.
In this chapter, the tables use metric units only.
Every morning, he still checks the mailbox before breakfast.
Until 1960, the old locomotive was painted bright green.
On the next page, only the first ten entries are printed.
After her morning swim, she walks home along the hard pavement.

notes: Card: ',' x16 after fronted reason phrases, ' convenience', ' suggest', ' implies'; the + pole takes commas after fronted when/as-soon-as clauses. Probe: 'For safety reasons,' 0.63, 'As the title suggests,' 0.54, 'Because of the heavy rain,' 0.26; 'When the bell rang,' 0.01, 'After a long day,' 0.06.
